questions.questionText: What is the first pillar of Islam?
questions.explanation: Shahadah is the primary foundational pillar of Islam.

questions.questionText: What does the first part of Shahadah testify?
questions.explanation: It declares that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah.

questions.questionText: Who is declared as the final messenger of Allah in Shahadah?
questions.explanation: Shahadah bears witness that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is Allah’s Messenger.

questions.questionText: What does 'La ilaha illallah' mean?
options: There is no god but Allah
questions.explanation: It is the fundamental declaration of Tawheed (Oneness of God).

questions.questionText: Reciting the Shahadah sincerely enters a person into?
questions.explanation: It is the testimony required to become a Muslim.

questions.questionText: What is the original language of the Shahadah?
questions.explanation: The Quran and the Shahadah are in Arabic.

questions.questionText: Who alone deserves to be worshipped according to Shahadah?
questions.explanation: Worship is dedicated strictly to Allah.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest sin in Islam (opposite of Shahadah)?
questions.explanation: Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is the unforgivable sin if not repented.

questions.questionText: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger and what of Allah?
questions.explanation: Muslims testify he is the slave ('abduhu) and messenger of Allah.

questions.questionText: Belief in the Shahadah must be affirmed by the tongue and?
questions.explanation: True faith requires affirmation by the tongue and belief in the heart.

questions.questionText: How many daily obligatory prayers are prescribed in Islam?
questions.explanation: Muslims perform 5 obligatory prayers daily.

questions.questionText: Which prayer is offered right before sunrise?
questions.explanation: Fajr prayer is offered before dawn.

questions.questionText: What is the required ablution before Salah called?
questions.explanation: Wudu is required for ritual purity before prayer.

questions.questionText: Which direction do Muslims face during Salah?
questions.explanation: Muslims face the Kaaba in Makkah.

questions.questionText: What is the midday prayer called?
questions.explanation: Dhuhr is the prayer performed just after midday.

questions.questionText: What is the call to prayer called in Islam?
questions.explanation: The Adhan is called out to notify Muslims that it is time for prayer.

questions.questionText: Which prayer is performed just after sunset?
questions.explanation: Maghrib is the fourth obligatory prayer, prayed immediately after sunset.

questions.questionText: What is the weekly congregational prayer on Friday called?
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah replaces the Dhuhr prayer on Fridays and includes a sermon.

questions.questionText: What do we say when starting the prayer?
questions.explanation: Takbeer (Allahu Akbar) is used to commence the prayer.

questions.questionText: What is the physical act of prostration in prayer called?
questions.explanation: Sujud (Sajdah) is prostrating with the forehead touching the ground.

questions.questionText: What is the standard rate of Zakat on accumulated wealth?
questions.explanation: The standard Zakat rate is 2.5% on qualifying wealth held for a year.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum wealth threshold for Zakat called?
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum wealth required before Zakat becomes obligatory.

questions.questionText: Which group of people is eligible to receive Zakat?
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tawbah verse 60 lists the eligible categories for Zakat.

questions.questionText: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Zakat'?
questions.explanation: Zakat purifies one's remaining wealth and promotes spiritual growth.

questions.questionText: Is Zakat obligatory on a person who does not meet the Nisab?
questions.explanation: Zakat is only obligatory on those whose wealth reaches the Nisab.

questions.questionText: What is voluntary charity called in Islam?
questions.explanation: Sadaqah can be given at any time and in any amount.

questions.questionText: Which item is subject to Zakat?
questions.explanation: Personal necessities are exempt, but hoarded precious metals are subject to Zakat.

questions.questionText: When is Zakat al-Fitr mandatory to be given?
questions.explanation: It must be given before the Eid prayer at the end of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: Can Zakat be given to build a mosque?
options: No, it is for specific categories of people
questions.explanation: Zakat is primarily for the 8 specific categories mentioned in the Quran.

questions.questionText: How long must wealth be held above Nisab before Zakat is due?
questions.explanation: One full Hijri year (Hawl) must pass on the qualifying wealth.

questions.questionText: In which month is mandatory fasting observed?
questions.explanation: Fasting is mandatory during the month of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: What is the pre-dawn meal before starting a fast called?
questions.explanation: Suhoor is eaten before dawn to prepare for the fast.

questions.questionText: What is the meal eaten at sunset to break the fast called?
questions.explanation: Iftar is the meal eaten to break the fast at Maghrib.

questions.questionText: At what time does the fast begin?
questions.explanation: Fasting begins at true dawn.

questions.questionText: Who is exempt from fasting during Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Those who are ill or traveling are permitted to break their fast and make it up later.

questions.questionText: What is the special night prayer in Ramadan called?
questions.explanation: Tarawih prayers are held in congregation every night in Ramadan.

questions.questionText: What breaks a fast?
questions.explanation: Intentionally eating or drinking nullifies the fast.

questions.questionText: What is the Night of Power called?
questions.explanation: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months.

questions.questionText: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the 1st of Shawwal.

questions.questionText: Fasting teaches Muslims what virtue?
questions.explanation: The primary goal of fasting is to attain Taqwa.

questions.questionText: In which holy city is Hajj performed?
questions.explanation: Hajj is performed in and around Makkah.

questions.questionText: On which day of Dhul Hijjah does standing at Mount Arafah occur?
questions.explanation: Standing at Arafah (Wuquf) takes place on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah.

questions.questionText: What is the sacred state required for performing Hajj?
questions.explanation: Ihram is the sacred state entered into before performing Hajj or Umrah.

questions.questionText: Circling the Kaaba is known as?
questions.explanation: Tawaf involves circumambulating the Kaaba 7 times.

questions.questionText: How many times must a pilgrim perform Tawaf around the Kaaba?
questions.explanation: It is required to circle the Kaaba 7 times.

questions.questionText: Walking between the hills of Safa and Marwa is called?
questions.explanation: Sa'i commemorates Hajar's search for water.

questions.questionText: Stoning the pillars in Mina is known as?
questions.explanation: Rami al-Jamarat is the stoning of the devil.

questions.questionText: Which animal is commonly sacrificed during Hajj?
questions.explanation: Livestock like sheep, goats, cows, or camels are sacrificed.

questions.questionText: Which Eid is celebrated during Hajj?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Adha is the festival of sacrifice.

questions.questionText: How many times is Hajj obligatory for a capable Muslim in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: It is mandatory once in a lifetime if one has the physical and financial means.

questions.questionText: Tawheed is divided into how many main categories by scholars?
questions.explanation: Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah, Uluhiyyah, and Asma was-Sifat.

questions.questionText: What does Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah mean?
questions.explanation: It means believing Allah is the sole Creator, Provider, and Sustainer.

questions.questionText: Which form of Shirk completely takes a person out of the fold of Islam?
questions.explanation: Major Shirk nullifies faith.

questions.questionText: Belief in Allah's names and attributes falls under which category?
questions.explanation: It relates to Allah's unique Names and Attributes.

questions.questionText: What was the core message of all the Prophets?
questions.explanation: Every prophet was sent with the message of worshipping Allah alone.

questions.questionText: Which Surah is considered equivalent to one-third of the Quran due to its focus on Tawheed?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas purely describes the oneness of Allah.

questions.questionText: What is the condition of 'Yaqeen' regarding the Shahadah?
questions.explanation: Yaqeen means having absolute certainty in the declaration.

questions.questionText: Showing off (Riya) in acts of worship is classified as?
questions.explanation: Riya is considered Shirk al-Asghar (Minor Shirk).

questions.questionText: Who were the first people to be invited to the Shahadah by the Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: He started secretly with his closest associates like Khadijah and Abu Bakr.

questions.questionText: A person who rejects the Sunnah but claims to follow the Quran is violating which part of the Shahadah?
questions.explanation: The second part testifies Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger, making his Sunnah binding.

questions.questionText: How many conditions (Shurut) of the Shahadah are universally agreed upon by scholars of Aqeedah?
questions.explanation: They are Knowledge, Certainty, Acceptance, Submission, Truthfulness, Sincerity, and Love.

questions.questionText: The concept of 'Al-Wala wal-Bara' is closely linked to which part of belief?
questions.explanation: It means loyalty to Allah/believers and disavowal of polytheism.

questions.questionText: What does 'Tawheed al-Hakimiyyah' refer to in modern Islamic discourse?
questions.explanation: It refers to the belief that Allah is the ultimate Lawgiver.

questions.questionText: If a person claims a prophet came after Muhammad (PBUH), what is their status?
questions.explanation: Rejecting the finality of Prophethood nullifies Islam.

questions.questionText: According to the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools, how are Allah's attributes understood?
questions.explanation: They affirm the attributes but without anthropomorphism (Tashbih).

questions.questionText: The phrase 'Kufr duna Kufr' (minor disbelief) was famously used by which companion regarding ruling by other than Allah's law?
questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas used this to explain different levels of Kufr.

questions.questionText: What is 'Tawassul'?
options: Seeking a means of nearness to Allah
questions.explanation: Tawassul is using a permissible means to draw close to Allah.

questions.questionText: Which sect historically deviated by claiming that committing a major sin completely expels a person from Islam?
questions.explanation: The Khawarij held the extremist view of Takfir for major sins.

questions.questionText: What is the ruling on one who mocks an established part of the religion out of a joke?
questions.explanation: Mocking Allah, His verses, or His Messenger is an act of Kufr.

questions.questionText: What is 'Ilm al-Kalam'?
questions.explanation: It is the study of Islamic doctrine through dialectical methods.
